posts.title: Some Thoughts on the Flora Of South Texas After Seeing It in Mexico…
posts.description: In December I flew to San Luis Potosi and spent 12 days doing vigorous field botany throughout the states of San Luis Potosi, Querétaro, Hidalgo, Mexico, Puebla, and Oaxaca. This consisted of meeting up with two different friends that live there, going out every day and photographing, documenting and filming every wild plant species that I came into contact with. posts.title: GETTING NATIVE PLANT LISTS FOR YOUR REGION ON BPLANT.ORG
posts.description: Visit bplant.org and follow the link below. After arriving on the main page, click on “REGIONS”. You will arrive at a page with a map on it. Click on your region. You will then arrive at a map of your region with a diagram of subregions. Click on your subregion, then at the bottom of the page click on “list native plants”, and you will arrive at a page listing the genus and species and common name

posts.title: Visualizing the Urban Heat Island
posts.description: I found myself explaining the Urban Heat Island to a cop a few nights ago after a lady in the neighborhood called the cops on me for planting trees on city property next to her house. This is the second time this has happened to me in the town I live in, a region inhabited by a populace that I (only half-jokingly) frequently refer to as “ hating trees ”.
